report: Independent cross-chunk lemma consistency review: complete Ya-Sin draft
status: No required lemma field changes found
scholarlyReview: Pending. This AI consistency review does not approve any lesson for publication.
method: Read all725 occurrence Arabic/lemma/word-class/root rows individually in reading order, not only the variant groups.
Read assembly diagnostics, distinguishing actual lexical sameness from raw QAC grouping artefacts.
Checked all189 verb lemmas against effective lexemes after overrides; passive occurrences retain active dictionary citations rather than copying passive paradigm past forms.
Used Unicode NFC only for comparing lemma strings. No occurrence Arabic, lemma or other content was normalized or edited.
Confirmed that all21chunk ID/lemma sequences exactly match the assembled draft.

manuallyConfirmedWithoutMatchingActKey.decision: Correct active citation. The passive card explicitly identifies active ذَكَّرَ / يُذَكِّرُ in noteUrdu and evidenceEnglish; absence of a matching ACT key is not a wrong authored lemma.

diagnosticDispositions.decision: Accepted. Bare stems and fully declined citation forms identify the same lexeme; these differences do not justify changing correct content.

diagnosticDispositions.category: Canonical mark order in doubled and derived verbs
diagnosticDispositions.decision: Accepted. Fatha/shadda order differences normalize to the same NFC sequence and do not change the citation form.

diagnosticDispositions.category: Gender variants in repeated nominal material
diagnosticDispositions.decision: Accepted as requested. Feminine and masculine dictionary citations are valid; every occurrence explanation correctly identifies the actual feminine adjective. No wrong lexeme or different refrain meaning is introduced.

Accepted. Head-particle citations and fused particle/pronoun representations are permitted variants, including independent-pronoun citation of a suffix component. Prefix inclusion/omission alone does not identify a different lexeme.
Accepted. Conventional versus small-alif spellings preserve dictionary identity. The exact Quranic occurrence strings remain unchanged.
None|None|particle/pronoun groups combine unrelated constructions because their source has no stem lemma. They do not imply that the words require one shared headword.

diagnosticDispositions.category: Contextual noun citations outside variant groups
diagnosticDispositions.decision: Accepted. The dead-person singular, feminine dead-earth adjective, collective multitude and livestock collective are supported by source lemmas and their occurrence explanations.

diagnosticDispositions.category: Passive and opaque raw lemma labels
diagnosticDispositions.decision: Accepted. Active dictionary lemmas coexist correctly with passive occurrence morphology/cards. Raw labels based on imperfect or passive stems do not supersede verified citation fields.

limits: This is a lemma-identity and cross-chunk consistency review, not a new scholarly certification of every teaching claim.
Valid citation, tanwin, gender, fused-form and NFC-mark-order variation was accepted. Optional style homogenization was not proposed.
Only this report was written. No chunk, library, guide, metadata, registry or approval gate was changed. No external authoring CLI was invoked.
